findings.source_passage: I only had the dinner part, but pizza awaited me. Still, being among such a large crowd of my fellow humans was a bitter reminder of how normal my boring life was.
findings.why_it_matters: The two-beat ironic structure — the mundane comfort (pizza) set against the existential flatness — is voice-establishing for Miriam's dry self-deprecating register. The draft collapses it into 'reminded me how flat my life felt,' losing the pizza payoff and the comic rhythm.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the pizza beat and the 'how normal my boring life was' phrasing so both the humor and the self-awareness land as distinct, sequential observations rather than a single compressed clause.

findings.source_passage: His fingers were clammy like his skin didn't quite fit.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 7, after Blake extends his hand
findings.why_it_matters: This simile ('skin didn't quite fit') is the first foreshadowing detail about Blake's non-human nature and carries interpretive weight for the genre's supernatural reveal; it is also stylistically distinctive. Its absence removes the motif entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the exact simile — 'His fingers were clammy like his skin didn't quite fit' — when Miriam shakes Blake's hand.

findings.source_passage: The world sped by us as a shadow play of colorful lights and figures.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after 'I glanced out the window and sighed'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'shadow play' image is prosodically and rhetorically distinctive — it is the chapter's only lyrical register shift and contextualizes Miriam's sense of living at one remove from life. The draft replaces it with 'The city slid by in a blur of lights,' which is generic.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the draft's generic image with the source's 'shadow play of colorful lights and figures' to preserve both the lyricism and its thematic resonance.

findings.source_passage: I slapped a smile on my face and walked over to them.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Slapped a smile' is a small but characteristically physical, self-aware idiom that establishes Miriam's wry internal voice; 'pasted on a smile' is a near-synonym but slightly more clichéd.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer the source's 'slapped a smile on my face' to maintain the narrator's specific diction.

summary: Three medium-severity failures — loss of the 'skin didn't quite fit' foreshadowing simile, erasure of the pizza/boring-life two-beat ironic structure, and replacement of the 'shadow play' lyrical image — combine to trigger regeneration.
